solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Insolence and criticism? That's cosmetic

parts.note: lip is cheeky, insolent talk
stick is harsh criticism, as in 'taking stick'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether cheek and a telling-off count as make-up.
explanation.definitionFit: Lipstick is a colouring product applied to the lips, a classic item of make-up.

clue.text: Radical English newspaper dragged into deception

indicators.note: dragged into puts the letters inside the deception word

parts.note: a lie is a deception
FT is the Financial Times, this puzzle's own paper

explanation.surface: An English paper gets caught up in a deceit and is called extremist.
explanation.definitionFit: A leftie is a left-winger, someone with radical socialist politics.

clue.text: Ugly row has one making claim

parts.note: plain means unattractive
a tiff is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A nasty argument ends with someone demanding something.
explanation.definitionFit: A plaintiff brings a legal action, asserting a claim against another party in court.

clue.text: Habitual drinker wanting best beer — half only?

parts.note: top means best

indicators.note: half only says just the back half of the drinker's beer is used

parts.note: the word beer, of which only the latter half counts

explanation.surface: A regular drinker wants the finest ale but just a half pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half' looks like a half-pint measure; it takes half the word beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A toper is an old word for a heavy, habitual drinker.

clue.text: Bore on the Tube to have concern about Ed Davey?

indicators.note: about here means the concern word goes round the party piece

parts.note: care is concern
Ed Davey leads the Liberal Democrats, so he gives LIB

explanation.surface: A dull commuter on London's Underground worries about the Lib Dem leader.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube suggests the London Underground, but here it is a gun barrel or tube. Ed Davey leads the UK's Liberal Democrats.
explanation.definitionFit: Calibre is the internal diameter of a gun barrel or tube.

clue.text: Important books by Greek characters in test paper

parts.note: lit is short for literature, writing of lasting merit
mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet; mus is its plural

explanation.surface: Weighty volumes sit beside Greek letters on an exam paper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Literature' in its sense of works of lasting merit is what makes 'Important' fair here.
explanation.definitionFit: Litmus paper is the strip chemists dip to test whether a liquid is acid or alkali.

clue.text: Type of crime where Jacob keeps account?

definitions.text: Type of crime where Jacob keeps account?

parts.words: Type of crime where Jacob keeps account?
parts.note: the name Jacob has AC, the account abbreviation, inside the name of the biblical sufferer

explanation.walkthrough: Remove AC (account) from Jacob and you are left with Job; the account sits inside Job, hence the phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A robbery carried out with help from someone working on the premises is known by this phrase.

clue.text: Instant tea and fine coffee

parts.note: a mo is a moment, an instant
cha (char) is slang for tea

explanation.surface: Someone serves instant tea alongside good coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' suggests instant coffee, but it is a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a high-quality coffee, originally shipped from the Yemeni port of that name.

clue.text: Keep short jack for example in racing vehicle

parts.note: to stock is to keep in supply

indicators.note: short means the last letter is cut off

parts.note: a jack is a playing card

explanation.surface: A short car jack is kept in a racing car's boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jack' suggests the lifting tool for a car; it is the playing card.
explanation.definitionFit: A stock car is an ordinary saloon modified for track racing.

clue.text: European after decline means to raise standard

indicators.note: after places the European behind the word for decline

parts.note: to flag is to tire or decline
a Pole is a native of Poland

explanation.surface: A European's fall in fortune is offered as a way to lift standards.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a banner, and a pole with halyards is the device by which a banner is hoisted.

clue.text: Gypsy chorus to an extent used for classic film

indicators.note: to an extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Romany choir's song features, in part, on a famous film soundtrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Psycho is Hitchcock's 1960 thriller, a landmark of cinema.

clue.text: Low resistance when rocketing in space

indicators.note: rocketing upward in a down clue means the low sound and resistance are read from bottom to top together

parts.note: to low is to moo, as cattle do
R is the physics symbol for resistance

explanation.surface: Little drag as a rocket climbs into outer space.
explanation.definitionFit: Room means available area or capacity, as in 'room to move'.

clue.text: Private meal served without starter

indicators.note: without starter means the first letter of the meal is dropped, a pun on a starter course

parts.note: dinner is a meal

explanation.surface: A private dinner is served with no first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts or feelings are personal ones, kept hidden from others.

clue.text: Count with descendants, investment in claret made here?

indicators.note: with joins the two words side by side

parts.note: blood means lineage or family descent
to bank on is to count on

explanation.surface: A vampire Count and his offspring, with blood-red claret, suggest Dracula's lair.
explanation.walkthrough: Claret is old slang for blood, so blood deposited is an 'investment' in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Donated blood is deposited and stored there, as money is lodged in a financial institution.

clue.text: Inconstant female facing crisis where power's out

indicators.note: facing puts the female letter in front of the rest
power's out says the power letter is removed from the crisis word

parts.note: a pickle is a fix or tricky situation
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A woman confronting a blackout emergency proves changeable.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone fickle changes loyalties or moods readily, lacking steadiness.

clue.text: With UK reel, triple forte could cause commotion

indicators.note: could cause says the letters will be rearranged to create something new

parts.note: fff is the musical marking for fortississimo, very loud

explanation.surface: A British dance played extremely loudly might cause a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A kerfuffle is a fuss or disturbance, a minor uproar.

clue.text: Killer led by pack around island

indicators.note: led by puts the reversed word before the killer
around turns the packing word back to front

parts.note: to jam is to pack tightly
the orca is the killer whale

explanation.surface: A predator heads a pack wandering round an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Majorca is the largest of Spain's Balearic Islands in the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Bring up subject of suffering and make trouble

parts.note: to raise a subject is to bring it up
hell is the place of eternal torment

explanation.surface: Mentioning someone's pain causes a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: RAISE CAIN fits the definition too, but Cain is not a subject of suffering.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise hell is an idiom meaning to cause a loud disturbance.

clue.text: Constitutional asset with crook entertaining Commons and Lords?

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the other letters within

parts.note: aslant means at an angle, crooked
HP stands for the Houses of Parliament

explanation.surface: A political crook is admitted to Parliament as a constitutional benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Constitutional' suggests the British constitution, but a constitutional is a walk taken for health.
explanation.definitionFit: An ashplant is a walking stick cut from an ash sapling, useful on a stroll.

clue.text: Son with slight temperature avoided species of crocus

indicators.note: avoided tells us the temperature letter is left out

parts.note: an affront is a slight or insult

explanation.surface: A son, ill with a mild fever, stayed away from some flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slight temperature' looks like a mild fever; 'slight' is the insult and 'temperature' is only T.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron, the spice, comes from the stigmas of the autumn crocus Crocus sativus.

clue.text: Lift to floor for enthusiasts

indicators.note: lift in a down clue means read the word from the bottom up

parts.note: to floor someone is to stun them

explanation.surface: Fans take the lift down to a particular storey.
explanation.definitionFit: Nuts means devotees or fans, as in 'health nuts'.

clue.text: Husband unknown: wife-to-be almost getting cross

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown

indicators.note: almost says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a bride is a woman about to marry

explanation.surface: A bride gets angry that her husband is a stranger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' reads as angry but is the noun: a crossbreed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is the offspring of two different breeds or species, which is what a cross means.

clue.text: All awry Spooner's much more important

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words are swapped

parts.note: way means far or much, as in 'way better'
higher means of greater rank, and it is said like hire

explanation.surface: Something is in a mess, and it matters a lot more.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the starts of WAY HIGHER gives the sound of HAY WIRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Going haywire means becoming chaotic or out of control.

clue.text: Carefree bachelor having much flexibility

parts.note: lithe means supple, very flexible

explanation.surface: A single man is relaxed and very supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means happy and untroubled, showing no worries.

clue.text: Blocks standard question — expert finally brought in

parts.note: par is the standard or norm

indicators.note: brought in places that letter inside the question word

parts.note: a query is a question

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of expert

parts.note: the word expert, whose last letter is used

explanation.surface: Someone stonewalls a routine question until a specialist is called.
explanation.definitionFit: Parquetry is flooring of wooden pieces laid in a geometric pattern.

clue.text: Run, with Russian runner, for country

indicators.note: with joins the pieces side by side

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
the Ural is a river in Russia, and a river runs

explanation.surface: An athlete jogs alongside a Russian sprinter for their nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Russian runner' sounds like an athlete; it is a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Rural describes the countryside, as opposed to the town.

clue.text: Suggest a magical formula

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to imply or signify

explanation.walkthrough: The verb sense of 'suggest' is the less obvious one.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to imply something will follow and words of incantation chanted by a witch.

clue.text: Ears ruptured — pressure found inside Prince Harry?

indicators.note: found inside places that letter within the jumbled letters
ruptured means the letters are broken up and reordered

parts.note: the word ears, rearranged
P is the physics symbol for pressure

explanation.surface: Burst eardrums from pressure in the prince's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Harry called himself 'the spare' to his brother the heir, and used it as his memoir's title.
explanation.definitionFit: As the younger son, Harry was the backup heir, an extra in reserve.

clue.text: Marketing division cut loose

parts.note: an ad is a piece of marketing
a rift is a split or division

explanation.surface: A firm's marketing department is severed from the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat cut loose drifts freely without mooring, so it is unattached.

clue.text: Fine malt drunk in Strand

indicators.note: drunk shows the words fine malt are muddled up, as if intoxicated

explanation.surface: Good whisky is downed on the Strand, the London street.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strand' suggests the London thoroughfare but is a thread.
explanation.definitionFit: A filament is a very thin thread or fibre, like a single strand.

clue.text: Informant perhaps in bank job

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who tells, a narrator or informer
second meaning: a bank clerk who handles cash

explanation.surface: A police source may be the inside man on a bank robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bank job' suggests a robbery, but here it is simply a post in a bank.
explanation.definitionFit: A cashier at a bank counter is called this, and so is anyone who relates or recounts something.

clue.text: Morning call: about to ring woman snake tempted, unfortunately

indicators.note: to ring means to encircle the other letters

parts.note: re means about or concerning
Eve was tempted by the serpent in Eden
ill means unluckily, as in ill-fated

explanation.surface: An early phone call concerns the woman the serpent misled.
explanation.definitionFit: Reveille is the bugle signal that wakes soldiers at dawn.
